title: Evaluation of binaural spatial enhancement for bilateral hearing aid users with severe-to-profound hearing loss.
summary: Despite wearing hearing aids, many people with severe to profound hearing loss still find it difficult to understand speech in challenging listening situations, such as in a cafeteria. A newly developed hearing aid module for sound processing enables better separation of sound sources and is thus intended to facilitate speech comprehension in situations with a lot of background noise. The study aims to investigate how well this new component works in everyday life for people with bilateral severe to profound hearing loss.

interventions.name: For the 4-week study period, participants will receive hearing aids equipped with a novel algorithm designed to better filter out background noise (the Binaural Spatial Enhancement (BSE) algorithm). criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
At least 6 months of experience with hearing aids 
Postlingual onset of severe hearing loss (≥ 4 years) 
Tone audiometric threshold between 60 and 90 dB HL for frequencies below 1 kHz 
Good knowledge of German 
Use of the study hearing aids in daily life during the two two-week practice phases.
Exclusion criteria:
Inability to follow the study procedures (e.g., due to language barriers, mental health disorders, dementia) 
Current or planned pregnancy  
Acute tinnitus lasting less than 3 months 
Infection of the external auditory canal or middle ear 
Acute vertigo
